title: Book Two · Chapter 22: Two Readers for One Story
story:
On Monday, Miss Wu brings a stack of story sheets to class.

She puts them on her desk. Leo leans forward. Ronan tries to see the top sheet too, but there is another book over it.

“These are for tomorrow,” Miss Wu says.

“Can we choose one now?” Leo asks.

“Not yet. Today we need to talk about the work.”

Each pair will read one short story. The two children will read quietly first. Then they will tell the story to each other. Next Monday, they will share it with the class.

“Do we stand at the front?” Ronan asks.

“You will stay by your desks. This is our reading lesson.”

“Are all the stories the same length?” Ronan asks.

“Some are longer.”

“Can I have a long one?”

“I will choose the pages tomorrow.”

Ronan looks at the stack again. He wants a long page. A long story will need more words, and he can read quickly. He puts his hand near the top sheet, then brings it back to his own desk.

Miss Wu points to the three questions on the board.

Who is in the story?

What happens first?

What happens next?

“We need clear answers,” she says. “You may use the page.”

Ronan looks at Leo. He remembers the train book. He and Leo read it together. He wants to read as quickly as Leo.

“Can we choose our partners?” he asks.

“I will arrange the pairs tomorrow.”

Leo turns to another child. They begin to talk about a book near the window. Ronan looks back at the questions.

Miss Wu holds up a small blank card.

“You can put three short notes here. You can draw small marks too. Do not copy the whole story onto the card.”

Mei raises her hand. “May I make a page about my own book?”

“Yes. Finish your reading task first. Then we can look at your page.”

Ronan turns to her. “Will you draw our story too?”

“I have my own page,” Mei says. “You can draw yours.”

He wants just one little picture. Her pencil is already moving over her own paper. He takes out his ruler instead.

Jun is at the next desk. He draws three empty boxes on a scrap.

“People, first, next,” he says.

“That looks easy,” Ronan says.

“The boxes are easy. We need the story.”

At break, Ronan walks to the book corner. A small child is reaching for a book on the high part. Ronan offers to get it.

“This one?”

“No. The one beside it.”

Ronan takes the right book down. He gives it to the child and leaves the other books in place.

Leo calls from the door. There is time for a short game outside.

They use the cloth ball. Leo throws it too high on the first turn. It lands on the low window ledge. Both boys look up at it.

“It is reading now,” Leo says.

Miss Wu opens the window from inside. She picks up the ball and hands it to them.

“Then it needs to finish before the bell.”

They move further from the window. This time Ronan catches the ball. He throws it low enough for Leo.

Back in class, the story sheets are still on the teacher's desk. Ronan wants the first turn tomorrow. He writes the three questions in his exercise book. He leaves a wide space under each one.

Jun checks his own little boxes. Mei closes her drawing book. Miss Wu puts the sheets away and begins the next lesson.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- pair＝两人一组
- partner＝搭档
- arrange＝安排
- ledge＝窗台凸出的边缘

## 理解问题

1. 双人任务有哪些具体步骤？
2. Mei为什么没有替Ronan画图？

## 从认词到读句子

正文原句：*The boxes are easy.*

**The boxes / are / easy.**

这些格子／是／容易画的。下一句才说明：他们还需要拿到故事。
